title: Watching macro_rules! expand
subtitle: Pick an invocation and step through matching and transcription

presets.label: hashmap!
steps: The parser sees a path, a ! and a delimited token tree. The contents are not parsed as an expression yet: they are just tokens handed to the macro.
Arms are tried from top to bottom. The first matcher () only accepts an empty input, so it fails and the next arm is tried.
The second matcher fits. $( … ),+ means "one or more, separated by commas", and $(,)? tolerates a trailing comma.
Each repetition binds $k and $v as expr fragments. A fragment is parsed as a whole AST node, so 2 + 2 would be bound as one expression, not three tokens.
The transcriber is copied out. $( map.insert($k, $v); )+ repeats once per captured pair, in order.
The result replaces the invocation. Thanks to hygiene, this map lives in the macro's own syntax context: it cannot clash with a map variable at the call site.

presets.label: count! (recursive)
steps: count! receives three token trees: a, b and c. They don't need to be valid expressions: tt accepts anything.
The input is not empty, so the base case () fails.
$head:tt takes the first token tree, $($tail:tt)* captures whatever is left. The output contains another count! call.
Macro output is expanded again, so the recursion continues with b c.
One more round: $head is c and $tail captures nothing.
The empty input finally matches the base case. Constant folding turns the sum into 3 at compile time. Recursion depth is capped by #![recursion_limit] (128 by default).

presets.label: no match
steps: Same hashmap! macro, but the caller wrote : instead of =>, as in a JSON or Python dict.
The empty matcher fails, as before.
The second arm starts well: "ada" is a valid expr and binds to $k. Then the matcher expects the literal token => and finds :.
No arm is left, so expansion fails with a compile error pointing at the unexpected token, plus a note on what the matcher wanted. Macro errors are compile errors, never runtime surprises.
